faq_items.question: How do I meal plan lunch for a week?
faq_items.answer: Choose one planning day, pick 3 to 5 lunches you actually like, and assign each weekday one: two make-ahead meals, two five-minute assemblies, and one leftover day. Batch the shared components in about an hour, then add only the missing ingredients to your grocery list.

faq_items.question: What are the best make-ahead lunches for work?
faq_items.answer: Grain bowls, mason-jar salads with dressing on the bottom, wraps stored with fillings separate, and portioned soups or chili hold up best for three to four days. Keep wet and dry components apart and combine the morning-of so nothing turns soggy before you eat it.

faq_items.question: How much money can meal planning lunch save?
faq_items.answer: Swapping a roughly $12 daily takeout lunch for prepped meals at about $3 a serving saves close to $45 a week per person — over $2,000 a year for one adult. Lunch is the meal most often bought out, so planning it returns the biggest savings of any meal.

faq_items.question: How do I keep packed lunches from getting boring?
faq_items.answer: Build every lunch from a base, a protein, two vegetables, and one punchy element — a sauce, pickle, or nuts. Swap just the punch (pesto, tahini, salsa) and the same base feels new. Theme your days and pack a crunchy item with a soft one to keep texture interesting.

faq_items.question: Can I reuse a printable lunch planner each week?
faq_items.answer: Yes. Print a fresh copy weekly if you like the clean-slate feeling, or slip one sheet into a plastic sheet protector and fill it in with a dry-erase marker to reuse indefinitely. Either way, keep it on the fridge beside your dinner plan so the whole day is visible.
